newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Labor replacement for Australia's Colston - opp'n.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Labor replacement for Australia's Colston - opp'n.

text.p: Australian opposition parties said on Monday that under the constitution independent Senator Mal Colson should be replaced by a member of the Labor party.
The Australian Democrats and Labor rejected Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge's claims that Colston should be replaced by an independent senator in the upper house of federal parliament.

"Senator Colston was an endorsed candidate for the Labor Party and publicly represented himself to be one and there are members of the Labor Party available to fill a casual vacancy," Australian Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot told Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.
"Therefore the vacancy should be filled by a member of the Labor Party. That's what the constitution says," Kernot said.
"What Premier Borbidge is saying is a deliberately mischievous and has the potential for destabilising federal government," she said.
Labor's Attorney-General spokesman, Nick Bolkus, said Borbidge's challenge to the constitution could invite a High Court ruling.
"In this particular case it's an example of the mischief making and the constitutional buffoonery that Premier Borbidge is indulging in," Bolkus told ABC radio.
"The Opposition could very quickly go to the High Court and get a ruling," Bolkus said.

Colston, who defected from the Labor Party in August, is being examined by the Australian Federal Police over allegations that he misused an expense allowance and gave government-paid jobs in his office to relatives who did not work.
Colston is one of the two independents in the Senate who have routinely supplied the two votes that the Liberal-National government needs to get contentious legislation through the parliament.
